title: Senior AI Engineer, Agents & Applications
description:
Firmus Technologies 

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability. 

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud 

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Why Firmus? 

As an NVIDIA Cloud and Engineering partner in Asia Pacific, you will gain skills, experience, and exposure across the AI industry and be part of shaping what this industry looks like for decades to come.

We are founder-led, not a big corporate. Decisions happen fast, our leaders are accessible, and there's minimum bureaucracy between you and the work. Ownership comes early. Whatever your role, you will have a direct line to outcomes, helping shape how the business grows as we scale nationally across a long-term, large-scale roadmap. 

Work alongside founders and experts in AI infrastructure, energy systems and next-generation compute.

What we build here has impact beyond the business. Our AI Factories are designed to operate as assets to the energy grid to actively strengthen the communities and regions they operate in rather than drawing from them.

Considering applying? You don't need a perfect background to join our team. If you're driven and curious, there's a path for you. We back our people to grow into new domains and take on challenges beyond their previous experience.

Role Summary 

The Senior AI Engineer (Agents & Applications) will design, build, and operate production-grade agentic systems that coordinate, optimize, and automate decision-making across the design-build-operate lifecycle of AI factories. The role is a core contributor to the AI & Applications team’s Model-to-Grid product, connecting models, inference endpoints, benchmark intelligence, validated workload recipes, job-scheduler decisions, infrastructure telemetry, AI-factory operations, and grid-related constraints into safe, explainable, and measurable workflows.

The role will build more than conversational co-pilots. It will create agentic applications that ingest and reason over time-series telemetry, logs, traces, events, scheduler state, benchmark results, configuration data, operational documentation, incident records, and multimodal sources where appropriate. These applications will help engineers, operators, and customers move from observation to diagnosis, recommendation, planning, simulation, controlled execution, verification, and continuous improvement.

The engineer will define and implement the underlying agent architecture and engineering framework: orchestration, state and memory management, retrieval, tool use, specialized sub-agents, evaluation, safety controls, human approvals, observability, and deployment. The role will use fit-for-purpose self-hosted and external model endpoints, with close integration to the team’s inference platform.

Key Responsibilities 

- Design, build, and operate agentic applications supporting AI-factory planning, commissioning, validation, workload onboarding, benchmark analysis, model and recipe optimisation, scheduling, operations, maintenance, incident response, and continuous improvement.

- Define reference architectures for single-agent, multi-agent, workflow-based, eventdriven, and human-in-the-loop agentic systems.

- Build orchestration workflows using appropriate agent frameworks and libraries, such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Microsoft AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, PydanticAI, Haystack, DSPy, or equivalent custom-built frameworks.

- Select the appropriate architecture for each use case rather than applying multi-agent 
patterns by default:

- Deterministic workflow and state-machine architectures for repeatable, high-confidence operational processes.

- Planner-executor architectures for decomposing complex investigation, planning, and remediation tasks.

- Supervisor-worker or manager-worker architectures for coordinating specialist domain agents.

- Router architectures for selecting the right model, tool, knowledge source, workflow, or specialist agent.

- Reflection, critic, verifier, or judge patterns for quality assurance, validation, and safety checks.

- Event-driven architectures for responding to telemetry anomalies, workload failures, scheduler events, benchmark regressions, and operational alerts.

- Human-in-the-loop architectures for high-impact recommendations, privileged actions, or changes to production environments.

- Build specialist agents for relevant Model-to-Grid and AI-factory domains, such as:

- Benchmark-analysis and performance-diagnosis agents.

- Workload recipe and runtime-configuration recommendation agents.

- Inference-endpoint selection, capacity, and optimization agents.

- Kubernetes and job-scheduler diagnostic agents.

- GPU-topology, network, RDMA, storage, and utilization-analysis agents.

- AI-factory health, capacity, maintenance, and operational-triage agents.

- Documentation, knowledge, incident-review, and runbook-execution assistants.

- Thermal domain specific monitoring and optimization agents.

- Power domain specific monitoring and optimization agents.

- Grid-integration specific monitoring and optimization agents.

- Develop the intelligent coordination layer for Model-to-Grid, enabling agents to reason across model characteristics, inference and training configuration, validated recipes, GPU resources, topology, scheduling policies, network and storage performance, capacity, power, thermal conditions, health signals, and operational constraints.

- Build Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines using a combination of vector retrieval, hybrid search, metadata filtering, reranking, structured-data queries, graphbased retrieval where valuable, source attribution, and permission-aware access controls.

- Use tools such as pgvector, OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone, Qdrant, Neo4j, or equivalent data and retrieval platforms as appropriate to the product architecture and deployment environment.

- Design knowledge-ingestion pipelines for documentation, runbooks, ticketing systems, configuration repositories, benchmark reports, experiment records, cluster state, telemetry catalogues, incident reports, and approved internal knowledge sources.

- Build data and context pipelines that combine unstructured knowledge with structured operational data, including metrics, logs, traces, events, time-series databases, scheduler queues, job states, resource inventories, and configuration-management data.

- Integrate agents with governed tools and APIs, including Kubernetes, proprietary scheduler services, observability platforms, benchmark services, inference endpoints, configuration repositories, CI/CD pipelines, ticketing systems, workflow engines, 
databases, and operational tooling.

- Define tool contracts using structured input and output schemas, typed interfaces, validation, retries, idempotency controls, rate limits, timeouts, circuit breakers, approval requirements, and detailed audit logging.

- Build robust agent harnesses that provide context assembly, model routing, prompt and policy versioning, structured output handling, memory management, state persistence, retries, failure handling, task recovery, escalation, and end-to-end tracing.

- Implement short-term task memory, long-term user or operational memory where permitted, episodic memory for prior investigations or incidents, and semantic memory based on approved knowledge stores; apply retention, access-control, and datagovernance requirements to each.

- Implement model-routing and fallback strategies across self-hosted inference endpoints and approved external models, selecting models according to task complexity, latency, cost, context-window requirement, tool-use capability, privacy needs, and reliability targets.

- Partner with the Self-Hosted Inference Platform & Optimization team to ensure that agentic applications have suitable endpoint profiles for planning, reasoning, embeddings, reranking, summarization, classification, tool use, multimodal analysis, and high-throughput operational workflows.

- Build agent workflows for detection, diagnosis, recommendation, planning, action simulation, controlled execution, verification, and learning loops.

- Develop offline replay, simulation, shadow-mode, and what-if evaluation capabilities to validate recommendations before allowing actions in production—especially for scheduler policies, workload placement, runtime changes, capacity decisions, and operational remediation.

- Design human approval and policy enforcement workflows that clearly present an agent’s evidence, recommendation, expected impact, proposed action, confidence, risk classification, authorization scope, and rollback option.

- Work with the Security Engineer to implement defense-in-depth controls against direct and indirect prompt injection, insecure output handling, excessive agency, unsafe tool use, data leakage, cross-tenant exposure, privilege escalation, credential misuse, unauthorized actions, and insufficient auditability.

- Use policy engines, guardrail frameworks, structured output validation, content and tool filters, permission checks, sandboxing, and allowlisted action patterns to ensure that agent behavior remains bounded and trustworthy.

- Implement agent observability using tracing, metrics, logs, prompt and model version tracking, tool-call records, evaluation results, token and cost tracking, user feedback, incident evidence, and action audit trails.

- Build and maintain evaluation frameworks using automated tests, curated test sets, simulation, replay, benchmark tasks, regression suites, model-based evaluators, human review, and operational-outcome measures.

- Evaluate agents on task completion, factuality, groundedness, retrieval quality, diagnostic accuracy, recommendation quality, tool-selection accuracy, tool-execution correctness, policy compliance, latency, cost, safety, and user or operator satisfaction.

- Partner with the Kubernetes and custom scheduler team to consume and explain queue state, placement rationale, topology information, capacity signals, workload lifecycle events, policy outcomes, and performance data.

- Partner with the Model-to-Grid product, inference, Platform, SDI, Security, UX, and global operations teams to turn agent capabilities into clear product workflows, production releases, runbooks, and measurable user and operational outcomes.

Skills & Experience 

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years building AI/ML applications, distributed systems, automation platforms, data products, or production workflow systems.

- Demonstrated experience delivering LLM-powered, agentic, retrieval-augmented, decision-support, or operational-automation applications into production.

- Strong Python expertise, including experience with FastAPI or comparable API frameworks, asynchronous programming, event-driven services, distributed task execution, data pipelines, and API integration

GPS goes dark. Signals get jammed. Most drones fall out of the sky. Ours don't. 

Soron Systems is building the navigation brain for autonomous drones that operate where GPS can't be trusted: contested airspace, indoor environments, and GPS denied zones. Born out of cutting edge research at TU Dresden, we've already flown our system under active jamming conditions and proven it works. title: AI Engineer (AI & GenAI) - Finance Domain

description:
Dans le cadre de l’ouverture d’un poste en CDI, nous recrutons un.e AI engineer , basé-e au choix à Lille ou Paris.

🚀 CONTEXTE & ENJEUX STRATÉGIQUES

Au sein de Decathlon Digital, l'équipe Finance Data engage une initiative majeure : transformer les métiers de la finance par l'intégration de l'IA Générative et Agentique.

Face à la fragmentation des analyses exécutées par la fonction FP&A, notre ambition est de construire des solutions plus standardisées avec l’appui de l’IA. Il s'agit d’implémenter des couches d'intelligence centralisées et agnostiques des outils, capable d'interagir avec l'ensemble de notre infrastructure (Workday, Data Lake, EPM, ...) pour faire évoluer nos interfaces d'une logique de consultation vers une logique d'action.

Dans ce cadre, nous développons des débriefs de performance financière générés par l’IA pour toutes les activités de l’entreprise. Il aide nos collaborateurs et managers à accéder instantanément à une information fiable et sur laquelle ils peuvent prendre des décisions.

Déjà déployé avec succès en France, Espagne, Italie et Belgique, ce projet est le premier d’une série à venir.

Pour mener ce projet, nous ne recherchons pas uniquement un.e développeur.se, nous avons besoin d'un.e " Builder " : un.e personne capable de traduire un besoin métier en solution technique, de l’implémenter, la qualifier, la déployer et la maintenir dans le temps.

🎯 VOTRE MISSION

Nous recherchons un(e) AI Engineer confirmé(e) pour participer activement à l'industrialisation et au développement de nos solutions d’IA pour les contrôleurs de gestion. Votre objectif est clair : transformer les besoins métiers en fonctionnalités IA fiables, mesurables et robustes.

Pour relever ce défi, vous évoluerez au sein d'un collectif dédié , en collaboration directe avec d'autres AI Engineers et un Product Manager. Cette organisation de proximité vous permettra d'assurer une synergie parfaite entre les enjeux produits, la roadmap et l'implémentation technique.

🛠 VOS RESPONSABILITES 

- Développement Agentique & Fonctionnalités

- Participer à l'extension des capacités de nos agents vers des actions d'écriture (write actions) en implémentant notamment des protocoles de tool-calling (MCP - Model Context Protocol) et des communications inter-agents (A2A).

- Contribuer à l'optimisation des coûts, de la latence et de l'efficacité globale du système en lien avec les équipes Plateforme et Infrastructure.

- Qualité, Évaluation & Observabilité (LLMOps)

- Développer et maintenir la couche de qualité de nos pipelines (Databricks / Vertex AI Search / Discovery Engine).

- Assurer le grounding (ancrage) des réponses et la vérification des citations pour garantir la traçabilité vers une source de vérité.

- Mettre en place des pipelines d'observabilité robustes pour l'évaluation online et offline (OpenTelemetry, MLflow, Langfuse).

- Coder des évaluateurs automatiques pour itérer sereinement et prévenir les régressions avant chaque mise en production.

- Intégrer des garde-fous (guardrails) pour protéger le système et les utilisateurs contre les hallucinations et les erreurs.

- Sécurité, Cloisonnement & Déploiement International

- Isolation & Multi-tenancy : Mettre en œuvre des stratégies de filtrage par métadonnées (metadata filtering) en base vectorielle et de cloisonnement (des index et/ou des modèles) pour assurer une étanchéité parfaite des données entre les différentes sociétés fiscales, entités légales et géographies de Decathlon.

- Support Multilingue : Contribuer à l'architecture d'internationalisation de nos solutions en adaptant les pipelines, l'embedding et l'inférence pour maintenir un haut niveau de performance et de pertinence sur une grande diversité de langues.

- Produit & Impact Business

- Aider à l'analyse des intentions des utilisateurs pour mesurer l'impact de nos produits

- Traduire, avec l'appui de la Product Manager, les enjeux métier en comportements de modèles et en métriques de succès.

🧠 PROFIL RECHERCHE

Nous recherchons un profil justifiant a minima d’une première expérience. 

- Expérience : Profil confirmé justifiant de plusieurs années d'expérience professionnelle en entreprise (hors stages et alternances) en AI Engineering, ML Engineering ou Software Engineering orienté IA. Vous justifiez également d'au moins une expérience concrète et réussie de mise en production d'un système GenAI ou agentique.

- Stack Technique : Solide maîtrise de Python, de l'écosystème GCP / Vertex AI + Databricks, et des frameworks d'orchestration (LangChain, LlamaIndex ou Google ADK).

- Expertise LLM & Agentique : Solide maîtrise des architectures RAG (recherche vectorielle, Vertex AI Vector Search, gestion avancée de métadonnées), mais surtout des concepts techniques agentiques : function/tool-calling, boucles de raisonnement (ReAct, etc.), orchestration de workflows multi-agents, structured output et gestion du contexte/mémoire.

- Qualité & Évaluation : Capacité à diagnostiquer une réponse incorrecte (problème de modèle, de retrieval ou de données) et appétence pour l'observabilité applicative (SQL / MLflow).

- Langues : Français courant obligatoire & anglais professionnel courant (environnement international).

Les plus : 

- Connaissance technique approfondie des protocoles A2A (Agent-to-Agent) et MCP.

- Compréhension technique des enjeux de sécurité (RBAC, ACLs, RGPD) appliqués aux LLMs.

- Connaissance des architectures microservices et conception d'APIs.

🎁 CE QUE NOUS PROPOSONS

- L'opportunité de développer un produit d'IA agentique de pointe avec un impact direct sur le quotidien des collaborateurs.

- Un environnement technologique premium (Stack Google Cloud / Vertex AI / Databricks).

- Une politique de télétravail flexible (2 jours par semaine en remote, le reste dans nos bureaux).

- Une culture du delivery axée sur l'autonomie, l'intelligence collective et la montée en compétences (accompagnement par un Lead, certifications, formations).

- Des avantages attractifs (primes mensuelles/trimestrielles, actionnariat salarié).

DECATHLON DIGITAL 

Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam. Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits.

Changeons la donne pour de bon. Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. C’est pourquoi nous nous engageons à bâtir un modèle technologique plus durable, en réduisant notre impact direct sur l'environnement, et en créant un espace sûr et inclusif pour apprendre et nous épanouir ensemble. Rejoins l’équipe et façonnons le futur du sport.

title: ML Intern: Optimization Quality & Monitoring
description:
Our common vision

Our mission is to help marketing teams unlock their full growth potential with AI. Our AI-powered attribution creates real transparency, showing how digital advertising investments perform across channels. On that foundation, we optimize budgets so our customers can sustainably grow their bottom line. We support leading European brands across e-commerce, telco, banking, insurance & energy, and many other industries in making their marketing smarter, more efficient, and more impactful.

About the role

Nexoya runs fully automated, AI-driven budget optimizations and simulations for enterprise marketing portfolios across many ad channels. Every result that reaches a customer must be correct, explainable and on time. As our ML Intern, you make sure it is: you monitor pipeline health, check the quality of predictions, optimizations and simulations, investigate anomalies and turn recurring manual checks into reliable tooling. You work closely with our ML engineers and Customer Success, and you see directly how your work shapes our customers' budget decisions.

Your responsibilities

Monitor the automation and assure result quality

- Monitor the automated prediction, optimization and simulation pipelines across customer portfolios and track run health, completeness and timeliness.

- Verify that predictions, optimization proposals and simulation results meet our quality standards before they reach customers: budget shifts, expected KPI changes, channel constraints and funnel-level effects.

- Investigate failed or unexpected runs, identify the root cause (data, configuration or model) and resolve it or escalate it with a clear diagnosis.

Assure the quality of results over time

- Define and maintain plausibility checks for optimization and simulation results, for example for budget planning, seasonal shifts or new channel tests.

- Make sure results are consistent and explainable, so that customers and account managers can trust them without manual checks.

- Compare optimized and simulated outcomes with realized performance, document deviations and feed the findings back to the ML team.

Safeguard data and model quality

- Monitor input data for gaps, anomalies and tracking changes that affect optimization quality.

- Track model fit and prediction accuracy per portfolio and flag degradation early.

- Maintain portfolio configurations such as funnel steps, constraints and target definitions together with the responsible teams.

Automate the operational workflow

- Replace manual checks with Python scripts, validation rules and alerts.

- Build and maintain dashboards that show run status, data health and model performance across portfolios.

- Write runbooks so that operational knowledge is shared, not held by one person.

The impact you will have

- Customers receive optimization proposals and simulations that are correct and delivered on time.

- Issues are caught before customers see them, not after.

- The time the ML team spends on operational work goes down measurably, because recurring steps are automated.

- Customer Success can trust automated optimization and simulation results without checking them by hand.

Your experience and skills

- Recently completed Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering or a related field.

- Solid Python skills, including pandas and NumPy, and comfort working with SQL.

- Good understanding of statistics and basic machine learning concepts such as regression, model evaluation and overfitting.

- A careful, structured way of working: you check results before you share them and you document what you do.

- Ability to explain technical findings clearly to non-technical colleagues.

- Fluent English, spoken and written, is a must.

Bonus points

- Experience with optimization methods, for example constrained or non-convex optimization.

- Familiarity with Marketing Mix Modeling, attribution or digital advertising metrics.

- Experience with data pipelines, scheduled jobs or monitoring tools.

- Experience with Git, Docker and cloud environments.

- Fluent in German or Italian.

Your future work life

- Purpose: Your work directly influences how enterprise marketers allocate their budgets.

- Responsibility: You own the quality of a defined part of our automation from day one, with a personal development roadmap and regular feedback.

- Learning: You work alongside experienced ML and data engineers on production systems, not on side projects.

- Culture: A transparent company culture at eye level, where every person is valued and supported.

- Strategy: You take part in shaping company strategy and culture during our quarterly Strategy Days.

- Events: Regular team events, on-site and off-site.

Application process

- Profile review and short phone screen

- Take-home case study

- Case discussion with the ML team

- On-site interview and team evaluation

title: Chief Technology Officer - US-Based
description:
About Toptal 

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce .

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it.

You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.

You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.

Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.

You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.

This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. 

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering 

- Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.

- Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.

- Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.

- Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability 

- Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.

- Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.

- Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

Platform and execution 

- Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.

- Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.

In the first week, expect to:

- Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.

- Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.

In the first month, expect to:

- Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.

- Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.

In the first three months, expect to:

- Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.

- Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

- Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.

- Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

- Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.

- Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

- 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.

- Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.

- Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.

- Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.

- Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.

- Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.

- You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.

- Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.

- Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.

- Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.

- Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

- Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.

- You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

- Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.

- Work independently with minimal supervision.

- Use all required digital collaboration tools.

- Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

title: Medior C++ Software Engineer
description:

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™) . This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

As a Medior C++ Engineer, you will take ownership of software components within our hardware-integrated systems. You will design, implement, and improve robust C++ software that interacts with multiple subsystems, and real-time environments. You will collaborate closely with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers to ensure system reliability, maintainability, and performance.

First months at Vitestro 

In your first months, you get to know Vitestro's software architecture, hardware-integrated systems, and development processes. You build an understanding of how our software interacts with different subsystems and start contributing to the design, implementation, and improvement of software components in modern C++ (C++17/20).

Working closely with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers, you become familiar with our state-machine-based logic, DDS communication protocols, and Linux and real-time environments. You contribute to debugging, automated testing, and code reviews while building the knowledge needed to take ownership of software components.

After your first month you will be able to contribute to the velocity of the team by working on new features in the scope of the motion team. You will be able to solve complex integration issues coming from production and the field.

This is what success looks like 

After 12 months, you have taken ownership of software components within our hardware-integrated systems. You confidently design, implement, and maintain robust C++ software that interacts with multiple subsystems and real-time environments.

You actively contribute to improving the existing software architecture, ensuring maintainability, scalability, and performance. You design and maintain structured state-machine-based logic, integrate evolving hardware components into the software stack, and contribute to system-level design discussions and technical decisions.

You work effectively with hardware engineers, systems engineers, and other software developers to debug complex issues across software and hardware boundaries. You have contributed to improving testability and automated verification strategies, actively participate in code reviews, and help raise software quality standards.

After your first year, you will own significant nontrivial features and parts of the code-base of the team. You will be a key knowledge holder of the implementation of the motion software unit as well as accuracy calibrations and verifications. You actively engage in building the roadmap for the coming years together with other engineers.

What You'll Bring: 

- Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

- 4–7 years of experience developing C++ software in a professional environment.

- Proven experience designing and maintaining production-level software systems.

- Strong proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20).

- Experience structuring code for maintainability and scalability.

- Experience with automated testing.

- Experience working in Linux environments.

- Strong debugging skills in complex systems.

- Proficiency with Git and collaborative workflows.

Nice to Have: 

- Experience designing and implementing state machines.

- Experience with hardware–software integration.

- Familiarity with DDS or similar pub/sub communication frameworks.

- Experience working in real-time or near real-time systems.

- Python scripting experience.

- Exposure to robotics or industrial communication protocols (EtherCAT, CANopen).

What we offer: 

- Competitive salary including pension plan

- 25 days of annual leave based on a full-time position

- Hybrid work model

- Working together in a high-skilled team with our home base in Utrecht

- Frequent out-of-work activities with our team, and annual company weekend away

- Annual training budget of €2000,-

- Opportunity to be key shaper of a new global industry niche: autonomous medical robotics

We offer an environment where you can make a lot of impact, as you are joining a growing scale-up in MedTech. Our team of driven and talented colleagues enjoys solving the challenges in developing, manufacturing, and completing our breakthrough medical device. While working in an open culture, we strive for excellence in all domains. We believe in taking courage and like to challenge each other. We learn and teach, regardless of age, nationality or gender.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. title: Critical Infrastructure Engineering Lead
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Our mission 

Serve as Mistral AI’s senior technical authority for critical electrical, mechanical and life-safety infrastructure across assigned colocation sites. Protect the availability of high-density AI compute by identifying technical risks before they become incidents, challenging infrastructure operating practices and verifying that power and cooling systems perform within agreed requirements.

Operating context & accountability 

Working with Engineering Operations leadership, IT Operations, hardware partners and colocation providers, you will provide hands-on technical assurance across a site or cluster. You will assess provider performance, advise on critical decisions, support incident response and ensure operational learning drives durable improvements. The role focuses on technical oversight and influence rather than direct management of the colocation provider’s maintenance workforce.

Technical assurance and operational risk 

- Own and maintain the site technical risk register, including electrical and mechanical single points of failure, maintenance exposure, redundancy limitations, cooling capacity, liquid-cooling interfaces and common-mode failure scenarios.

- Assess the resilience of utility connections, MV/LV distribution, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busways, protection systems, pumps, cooling plant, controls and monitoring against the contracted operating envelope.

- Review provider preventive maintenance strategies, schedules, critical asset condition and outstanding defects; identify maintenance deferrals and vulnerabilities that may affect AI compute availability.

- Critically review high-risk methods of procedure, electrical switching and isolation plans, planned impairments, work sequencing, contingency measures, rollback plans and restoration criteria.

- Validate the completeness and quality of technical documentation, including single-line diagrams, P&IDs, operating sequences, alarm matrices, capacity records, asset registers and operating procedures.

- Use BMS/EPMS trends, alarms, power-quality records and cooling telemetry to identify abnormal operating conditions, capacity constraints and deteriorating resilience before service is affected.

Incident response, investigations and reliability 

- Act as a senior engineering escalation point during major infrastructure incidents; rapidly assess failure domain, remaining redundancy, safety implications, likely IT impact and viable restoration options.

- Coordinate technical information across the colocation provider, Mistral IT Operations and OEM partners, ensuring accurate incident timelines, risk communication and controlled return to service.

- Review and challenge root-cause analyses, distinguishing immediate triggers from underlying design, maintenance, controls, process and organizational contributors.

- Define and follow up corrective and preventive actions, requesting evidence of implementation and verifying that recurring failure modes have been addressed.

- Identify systemic trends across sites and share lessons learned with engineering design, commissioning and regional operations teams.

- Support emergency response planning and tabletop exercises covering loss of utility, cooling failures, liquid leaks, fire/life-safety events and critical equipment failures.

Capacity delivery, commissioning and change control 

- Participate in design and constructability reviews for expansions, retrofits and new AI deployments; flag operational, maintainability and resilience concerns early.

- Review commissioning and integrated systems testing plans, including power transfers, redundancy scenarios, controls failure modes, cooling recovery and operational readiness criteria.

- Challenge test results and acceptance evidence against defined electrical, thermal and operational requirements; track unresolved technical issues through handover.

- Partner with IT Operations on rack power and thermal limits, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution unit boundaries, leak response and load-restoration dependencies.

- Assess proposed changes to critical infrastructure, including concurrent maintenance, controls updates and brownfield works; recommend safeguards and escalation where exposure is unacceptable.

- Provide technical coaching to internal stakeholders, contribute to engineering standards and support recruitment and knowledge sharing as the portfolio expands.

Success measures 

- Critical technical risks are identified early, prioritized and reduced through verified mitigation actions, supporting Mistral’s availability objectives.

- High-risk maintenance and infrastructure changes receive timely, evidence-based technical review with clear mitigations and escalation.

- Major incidents are diagnosed accurately, communicated effectively and followed by robust root-cause analysis and verified corrective actions.

- New and expanded capacity meets agreed redundancy, electrical, cooling and operational acceptance requirements.

- Repeat failures, unresolved high-severity defects and preventable technical deviations decrease over time.

Minimum qualifications 

- 5–7+ years in critical facilities engineering, commissioning, data center operations or technical assurance in high-availability environments.

- Strong practical knowledge of critical electrical infrastructure (UPS, generators, MV/LV distribution, switchgear and protection) and mechanical systems (cooling plant, pumps, controls and heat rejection).

- Ability to review single-line diagrams, operating sequences, technical procedures, maintenance plans, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses.

- Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure incidents and influencing external technical teams without direct line authority.

- Clear written and verbal English communication, sound judgment under pressure and willingness to travel and participate in incident escalation as needed.

Preferred experience 

- Full technical governance, multi-site operations or mission-critical facilities serving high-density AI/HPC workloads.

- Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility/technology cooling interfaces, water quality, leak detection and rack-level thermal management.

- Integrated systems testing, EPMS/BMS trend analysis, protection coordination, failure-mode reviews and cross-site engineering standardization.

- Experience partnering with hardware OEMs, design engineers, commissioning teams and infrastructure providers during live-site expansion.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

title: Senior Android Developer (f/m/d)
description:
adjoe builds the technologies behind mobile apps growth and monetization. adjoe Ads is our programmatic in-app advertising platform that seamlessly connects advertisers and publishers through direct integration of our Android and iOS SDKs. Every ad decision happens in under 200ms across 10 million daily users, powered by real-time bidding algorithms and user quality prediction models that match the right ad to the right user at the right moment.

Where 50 Billion Daily Predictions Begin

The User Experience team is the origin point of adjoe Ads. Everything the system knows about a user, every prediction the ML models make, every bid placed in an auction. It all starts with code this team ships.

The team owns two responsibilities. On the SDK side, a native Kotlin and Swift code runs inside hundreds of publisher apps. It participates in 120 million daily auctions , renders ad creatives across multiple formats, and captures the behavioral signals that power 50 billion predictions per day . The constraint that defines this work: you're executing inside someone else's app, on someone else's device, with zero tolerance for instability. Every ad impression has to feel native and fast to the user.

On the analytics side, the dashboards, investigation tools, and data frameworks that turn raw data into decisions: real-time revenue performance across active campaigns, infrastructure cost visibility, and data quality assessments. If a number matters to the business or to engineering, this team makes it accessible.

Your Mission & Who We Are Looking For: 

- Kotlin & Android Internals Expertise: You will own the core development and optimization of the adjoe Ads SDK, which runs inside hundreds of publisher apps. We are looking for someone with 8+ years of Android experience (or 3+ years specifically in SDK/library development) who works primarily with Kotlin and has a deep understanding of Android lifecycles, ProGuard/R8, and multithreading to ensure zero tolerance for instability on millions of devices.

- High-Performance Network Design: You will collaborate with backend teams to design APIs and capture behavioral signals that power 50 billion daily ML predictions. You need a strong track record in API design, maintaining strict backward compatibility for thousands of external integrators, and working with high-performance networking protocols like gRPC, Protobuf, Wire, and OkHTTP.

- Resource-Constrained Optimization: You will ensure every ad impression feels native and fast while participating in 120 million daily auctions. You must know how to design for minimal footprint, optimizing battery impact and memory usage, as your code executes directly inside someone else’s app and device.

- Data-Driven Observability: You will monitor, debug, and maintain SDK reliability at scale across millions of global users. You will leverage observability and data tools—including Sentry, Kibana, and AWS (S3, QuickSight, Athena)—to track errors, investigate SDK behavior, and turn raw data into clear engineering decisions.

- Build Automation & Delivery: You will maintain and improve our CI/CD pipelines to guarantee efficient, reliable SDK delivery. This requires hands-on experience with Gradle and GitLab CI to automate the testing, building, and packaging of our mobile libraries.

- Plus – AdTech & Low-Level Systems: It is a major plus if you bring experience in ad-tech or programmatic advertising (aligning products with IAB specifications). Additionally, experience with NDK/JNI (C/C++ interop on Android) or parallel iOS development experience is highly valued to help support our cross-platform ecosystem.

🌎 We welcome applications from talent worldwide and provide relocation support to Hamburg, Germany for those ready to join our team.

https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. Hiring: VIN Decode Engineer, Data Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Founding Engineer (dealer platform). TypeScript, Postgres, Cloudflare Workers. Full descriptions and apply: https://cardog.app/careers

title: Abuse Research Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

- Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

- FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. 

- Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. 

- Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. 

- Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. 

Who you are 

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

Minimum requirements

- 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains. 

- 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems. 

- B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines. 

- Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies. 

- Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

Preferred qualifications 

- Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing). 

- Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK. 

- Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn. 

- Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence. 

- Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale. 

- Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-abuse-research-engineer

title: Technical Co-Founder (AI Efficiency) @ AI Venture, Berlin
description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture 

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the results against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the best combination for each task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder was selected for Slush 20 Under 20, awarded by Anthropic, Slush, Index Ventures and Sifted. We closed our pre-seed round in two weeks and already have people waiting to use the product. We're now looking for a technical co-founder to help turn this opportunity into a company.

About the Role 

As Technical Co-Founder, you will lead the development of our AI efficiency engine, working alongside the founder to turn a compelling technical opportunity into a product.

At the heart of the role is a deceptively simple question: how can we make AI models deliver the same or better results at a fraction of the cost? 

You will explore approaches to model routing, fine-tuning, caching and inference optimisation, combining scientific curiosity with the ability to turn promising ideas into measurable improvements.

This is a role for someone who enjoys difficult technical problems, rigorous experimentation and challenging existing approaches. You won't be expected to build every part of the platform yourself. Working alongside our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, you will set the technical direction and focus your expertise where it creates the greatest impact.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. We're looking for someone who already operates this way, using coding agents and developing the workflows and harnesses that allow a small team to move exceptionally quickly without compromising technical quality.

Above all, this is a co-founder role. We're looking for someone who wants to take genuine ownership, work with relentless intensity and help build a company from its earliest stages.

What You'll Work On 

- Drive AI cost efficiency: develop approaches to reducing inference costs through model selection, routing, caching, fine-tuning, quantization and other optimisation techniques.

- Experiment and benchmark: design rigorous evaluations to understand the trade-offs between cost, quality and latency, turning technical insights into measurable improvements.

- Shape the efficiency engine: determine how closed and open-weight models can be combined and optimised to deliver the best outcomes for different tasks.

- Set technical direction: identify promising opportunities, make key architectural decisions and guide the founding engineers in bringing them to production.

- Push agentic engineering forward: use coding agents as a core part of your work and develop the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to operate with exceptional leverage.

- Build the company: work closely with the founder on technical strategy, attract exceptional talent and help shape the product and business.

About You 

You bring deep technical curiosity, scientific rigour and an entrepreneurial mindset. You enjoy getting into the details, testing hypotheses and finding approaches others might overlook.

We're particularly interested in people who bring:

- Deep expertise in AI efficiency: meaningful experience optimising the cost or performance of LLMs or other AI systems, with concrete results to show for it. Experience in inference optimisation, routing, fine-tuning or related techniques is particularly relevant.

- Strong technical foundations: a solid understanding of modern AI models, rigorous experimentation and the ability to translate research into practical improvements.

- An agentic approach to engineering: you actively use coding agents, know how to orchestrate them effectively and are excited by what small, highly leveraged teams can achieve.

- A co-founder mindset: you're resourceful, ambitious and comfortable with uncertainty. You take initiative, move quickly and want to build something from the ground up.

- Technical leadership potential: you have the judgement to make difficult technical decisions and guide others. Previous CTO or engineering management experience is not required.

We're more interested in exceptional depth in AI efficiency and the ambition to build a company than a conventional CTO background.

Fluent English is required; German is a plus.

Nice to Have 

- Experience with open-weight models, GPU inference or model serving.

As an Experimentation & Tracking Engineer, you will own web experimentation at Alma: the A/B tests we run on merchant websites, the measurement of what happens on our own website, and its continued development following our recent redesign.

Lead merchant experimentation from opportunity to readout

title: Product
description:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, to orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, to generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP. 

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

Why Product is the only role that sees the whole thing

"If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses.” - Henry Ford 

Our FDEs go deeper into a single customer than anyone else at Atira. What nobody can see from inside one account is the shape that all the accounts share. You hold the version of the problem that is bigger than any single customer's description of it, and you break it into steps small enough to ship every month.

Then you defend it. Every deployment produces requests: A few are the next platform feature, most are a customer-specific detour that should never be touched. You are the person who cares the most about consolidating solutions and has the technical depth to do something about it, which means you decide what comes in and what does not.

As Atira scales we build industry-specific pods: FDE, AE, BDR and Product Marketer, led by a GTM Engineer. Pods go deep. Product goes wide. Everything a pod learns has to end up in one platform, and you are the reason it does. Make sure we do not chase faster horses.

What you will do

- Own the problem, not the request. You understand which customer's ask is part of which bigger problem and you hold the maximum version of where this goes. Then you do the more challenging half: turning it into opinionated steps that ship, each one compounding into the next, so what we build becomes a staircase instead of a pile of features

- Decide what scales and what doesn't. You sit at the boundary between customer work and the core engineering team. You turn recurring patterns into features and you kill the rest. In an ideal world you are opinioonated on every FDE PR that touches shared code or introduces a customer-specific path

- Build the agents that make Atira work. You go deep on each customer's technical sales process, understanding it in all its details. You extend our harness to solve the most complex job functions of our users: how to configure machines according to the engineering experts, how to price large service agreements for billion dollar infrastructure projects, or how to automate the multi-stakeholder internal communication. And you can translate that into code

- Ship the platform end to end. Full-stack feature conceptualization and execution, from the harness through the UI a sales engineer actually uses

- Collect Feedback in front of the users that ultimately are your sounding board

What we are looking for

Taste, ownership, and systems thinking. You can build almost anything now, which makes judgment about what to build the bottleneck. You see the problem behind the request, you decide in the absence of a brief, you say no to founders and to customers with reasoning that survives the room, and you own the outcome including the downside.

Your profile 

- Systems thinking, in both directions. Upward: you find the problem behind the request and can hold a version of it bigger than what any single customer describes. Downward: you see the second-order effects, that one per-customer config field means a migration on every future deployment and one more thing every FDE explains in onboarding.

- Taste you can point at. You can show us things you have built and shipped that you are proud of, and a clear opinion on what you deliberately left out.

- Deep software engineering fundamentals underneath a native use of agents. Strong Python, TypeScript or a related language. You judge and ship production-grade code, and you can review someone else's. Practical exposure to AI engineering (agents, harnesses, evals, RAG), deeper system design understanding or infra knowledge

- Demonstrated ownership and initiative: a company you started, a leading role in a student initiative, an open-source project, a serious side build, or a role where you owned an outcome others would have delegated

- You get excited by complex hardware. You can explain in your own words why an agentic sales engineer at an ETO manufacturer is a business worth building, and what Atira is trying to become

What you'll get

- Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and architecture as well as work closely with customers

- Strong peers: work with people who have built and shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale before, and the chance to learn directly from them

- Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe's and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide

- Competitive salary & equity package and additional benefits including Wellpass, JobRad and company dinners

- Most importantly: collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function, but we will do so with modesty and integrity

What success looks like after a few months

- Someone new can hear you describe what we are building and walk away with the same picture the founders have, plus a clear view of which step comes next

- You have contributed your own thoughts to our general product vision and conceptualized a clear path forward to implement high prio features

- You have shipped full-stack features and agents into production that are used across multiple accounts, and every one of them came from a request that showed up at more than one customer

- The FDEs say the platform got easier to deploy, not harder

- Your no's carry as much weight as your yes's, with the founders and with customers

Je hebt minimaal 2 tot 3 jaar ervaring met data-engineering in productie en je denkt vanuit architectuur, niet vanuit losse taken. Verder: 

Wat we echt nodig hebben

Mooi als je dit meebrengt

title: AI Engineer (Agentic AI)
description:
Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we’ve been building that knowledge for 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. Other legal AI tools run on our data and software. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we’re also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax professionals don’t just get an answer, but an answer they’re willing to put their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Medior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD 

GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a useful answer. It does this with agents: specialised AI components that each handle part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can't just sound fluent. It has to be correct, and you must be able to see which source it comes from. This is not a pilot project: the platform runs in production and is used heavily every day.

As a medior, your focus is on building. You work independently, on challenges that come from customers and on challenges we spot ourselves. You break down a legal process, translate it into a technical process and work out how to best connect the pieces. Stuck on something? You say so, and your colleagues think along with you.

You build and improve the agents of GenIA-L and the way they work together.

You build and maintain our knowledge packages: for each legal article, an expert-validated set of commentary, case law, parliamentary history and practical interpretation. You also work on the pipelines that create these packages and keep them up to date.

You make quality measurable. With evaluation sets, observability and metrics, you show that answers, source attribution and reliability really improve. Not by gut feeling, but with evidence.

You build features for customers, such as analysing their own documents and new ways to search case law.

You work directly with editors and subject-matter experts, and check with them which parts of a legal question really matter.

You come up with and test ideas to make the product sharper or faster, and alternate AI experiments with back-end development.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

You have a realistic view of LLMs. You see what they can do, but you also know their weak spots. You enjoy following new AI developments, but you don't just follow the herd: you stay critical. You think in a structured way and can break a complex problem into smaller pieces. You work independently, take initiative when things are unclear and are eager to learn fast. And you enjoy working with lawyers and editors, because they know what a good answer looks like.

- You have several years of experience in software or ML engineering. Depth in recent projects counts for more than years.

- Strong experience in agentic AI. 

- You have good knowledge of Python and experience with relevant machine learning libraries.

- You have helped build an LLM application that runs in production. Not just prototypes, notebooks or courses.

- You have hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and LangChain, tool calling, MCP or comparable orchestration. Our entire product is built around this. Experience with only a simple search-and-answer (RAG) setup is not enough.

- You have measured the quality of an LLM system with evaluation sets or observability, and can give a concrete example. Experience with tools like MLflow and LiteLLM is a plus.

- You have back-end experience, including building REST APIs.

- You have experience in Kubernetes. Experience with Postgres is useful.

- Experience in a legal, tax or other knowledge-intensive domain is a plus.

WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR 

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the team works together at the office. What colleagues value most here: mutual trust, room to experiment, and a team that helps each other out when someone gets stuck.

- A place where you have influence from day one: on the approach, the processes, and the direction.

- Colleagues who deliberately chose Lefebvre Sdu over big tech jobs because here, they're building something that doesn't exist yet.

- Base salary between €4,477 and €5,793 per month, based on a 36-hour week, since that's full-time for us. Plus a lot of extra allowances (see below).

- A bonus tied to company performance: a fixed year-end bonus of 4% and profit sharing of up to 6%.

- 23 vacation days and a personal choice budget of 12%, of which 8% is holiday pay and 4% is freely allocable. Want more vacation? Just buy it.

- A bonus of up to 10% of your salary, based on company performance and individual performance.

- A solid pension plan through PGB, including supplementary partner insurance.

- Collective insurance plans.

- A travel allowance of €0.25 per kilometer or a public transport reimbursement, plus an attractive bike plan. For employees with a commute of less than 10 km or more than 60 km, we have an adjusted arrangement.

- Two days a week in the office in The Hague, within walking distance of Voorburg station. The rest of the week, wherever you work best.

- Room to grow: in your craft, in your role, in the organization.

WANT TO KNOW MORE? 

We'd love to tell you everything about the team and the role. Send us your CV and you'll hear from us within 2 working days. Any questions first? Text or call Nadine at 0628556265.

A reference check and a VOG (certificate of good behaviour) are part of the selection process.
